subject: Post-demo: log extract format and retention follow-ups
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Siva Narayanan <siva@acuityhealth.com>, Lauren Miles <lauren.miles@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: log extract format and retention follow-ups

Hi Siva / Lauren —

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the deep dive and the specific questions on who/what/when exports and retention windows. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the next steps and propose a minimal extract spec so your Security & Privacy team can validate whether it meets Acuity’s audit requirements.

Quick recap / asks:
- You wanted a sample extract showing access events for a 30-day window (who accessed records, which dataset/model, operation type, and exact timestamp).
- You asked about export formats (CSV vs JSONL), timezone handling, and whether our export includes entity IDs vs. pseudonymized identifiers.
- Retention: you mentioned policy requires 1 year for audit-ready logs and 7 years for certain regulated datasets — we need confirmation of the final retention classification for Redwood to propose retention settings.

Attached I’ve dropped a small sample CSV (who-what-when-sample.csv) and a short draft retention policy (pii-retention-policy-draft.docx) showing how Redwood’s exports map to common fields. Highlights:
- Default fields: timestamp (RFC3339), user_principal (email or service principal), action (generate/embeddings/read/admin), model_id, session_id, request_id, resource_id, region, request_payload_ref (pointer), response_token_count.
- Timestamps are exported in UTC by default; we can include an additional timezone column if required.
- We can provide either CSV or JSONL; JSONL preserves structured fields (e.g., nested resource metadata) if you prefer.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm the exact retention class for the datasets in scope (30-day sample vs. 1 year vs. 7 years).
2) Tell us whether you prefer CSV or JSONL for downstream ingestion (we can produce both).
3) If you need pseudonymization at export time (hashing IDs), say so and we’ll include a sample mapping.

I’ll loop Legal/Privacy at Redwood once you confirm retention and pseudonymization needs so we can draft a short attestation of fields included in the export.

Best,

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Siva Narayanan <siva@acuityhealth.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 17:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: log extract format and retention follow-ups

Diego — thanks for the quick follow-up and the sample. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Retention classes: for PHI-adjacent activity we require 7 years; for general application access logs 1 year; for admin & infra logs 3 years. We’ll confirm a final list but please assume conservative (7 years) until we confirm.

2) Format: we prefer JSONL for ingestion into our SIEM (Splunk/Phantom pipeline) — we need nested fields preserved, particularly for resource metadata and request payload refs.

3) ID handling: need pseudonymized user IDs in the export (one-way hash) with a separate key escrow option if we ever need to re-link (only available through a documented legal process).

4) Timezones: UTC is fine. Please include an event_received_at field in addition to the primary event timestamp to capture ingestion delay.

Can you confirm whether Redwood includes the raw request payload pointer (not the payload itself) and whether the export will include a field for whether the logged event contained PII (boolean flag) — that latter is important for our downstream retention rules.

If you can produce a 30-day sample JSONL payload tomorrow morning (UTC) that reflects the one-way hashed user IDs and the event_received_at field, that would be ideal.

Thanks — Siva
Siva Narayanan
Sr. Security Engineer, Acuity Health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Siva Narayanan <siva@acuityhealth.com>, Lauren Miles <lauren.miles@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: log extract format and retention follow-ups

Siva —

Thanks, that helps a lot. Quick answers inline and what we’ll deliver: 

- Raw request payloads: we do not include raw payloads in the standard audit export. We provide a request_payload_ref (signed URL or internal pointer) so you can retrieve it if you have permission — we can include a pointer_type field describing the retrieval mechanism.
- PII flag: yes — we can include a boolean field pii_detected (true/false) based on Redwood’s PII classifier at request time. Note: classifier is conservative; we'll provide thresholds and examples.
- One-way hashing: we can provide user_id_hashed using SHA256 with a per-customer salt. We will not provide the salt unless legally requested; we can support key-escrow workflows via an executed DPA amendment.
- event_received_at: we will include this for ingestion delta tracking.

Deliverables we’ll send by EOD Friday UTC (attached to this thread):
- 30-day JSONL sample (redwood-audit-export-spec-v1.json) showing nested resource metadata, event_received_at, pii_detected, and hashed user IDs.
- Export spec doc (we’ll attach a PDF if you want a printable version).

Marissa — can you confirm whether we need to escalate to Legal now for key-escrow language or wait until Acuity confirms which datasets require 7-year retention?

Thanks,
Diego
